package.name: dynrec
package.description:
A Python library for driving a running rosbag2_dynamic_recorder from a script, and for reading its bags back honestly afterwards.
`ros2 dynrec` covers the shell; this covers the supervisor. A mission script that changes what is recorded when the robot changes what it is doing should not be shelling out to a CLI and parsing its output, and it should not have to write seventeen service clients by hand either.
Talks to the recorder over its own rclpy context and its own executor thread, so it works equally in a plain script with no ROS of its own and inside a callback of the caller's node -- where spinning a node someone else's executor already owns would otherwise deadlock. That is the case this exists for: react to an event by changing the recording.
The modules holding the judgement -- how a recorder is identified, what `at` accepts, and which numbers the recorder cannot vouch for -- import no ROS at all, so they are testable without a graph and readable without one.
